changes.what: byte-identical copy of GeoGS's adapter (S1/geogs/source/GeoGS-official-adapters-v1, sha256 06510fab...): the projection matrix's P00, P11 = 2 fx / W, 2 fy / H and P02, P12 = (2 cx + 1 - W) / W, (2 cy + 1 - H) / H from the scene's jbgs_calibration.json (cx, cy in the rasterizers' pixel convention = the measurement's centre - 0.5), so the 3DGS rasterizer's ndc2Pix puts a point where the fork's camera does
loadCam returns maybe_calibrate_camera(Camera(...), args, cam_info) (training, evaluation and CDGS's render.py cameras)
readColmapCameras: K of the SfM-depth projection (the alignment targets) from jbgs_calibration.json instead of (W/2, H/2)

changes.order_4_2: input reading: prior depth incl. masking of no-hit pixels (order 5.5 2)
changes.what: a prior pixel without a hit (NaN, inf, <= 0) is left out: (i) of the alignment: its SfM target and weight are set to 0 before the weights' max-normalisation and the code's own 0.1 % prune (the code's existing mask = target > 0); (ii) of the aligned depth: set to 0 after the fit (the training loss's existing mask original_depth > 0); (iii) of the confidence map: jbgs_calculate_confidence_hit = the same Canny/Laplacian/Sobel features and weights 0.2/0.5/0.3 with every statistic (Laplacian max, each min-max, the final min-max) over the hit pixels, the Sobel input extended at no-hit pixels by the nearest hit pixel's depth (no artificial step at the end of the prior's coverage, as the image border), 0 at no-hit pixels; with every pixel hit it equals calculate_confidence. A view with no SfM target left on hit pixels after the code's own prune (the alignment would return NaN) gets no depth and no depth loss

optimize_depth keeps scale, shift, loss, SfM targets used, Adam steps (_JBGS_LAST); readColmapCameras logs them per training view with the hit share and weight 0.6 exp(-150 L) to <scene>/jbgs_alignment.json; JBGS_KEEP_ALIGN_ARRAYS=1 (checks only) keeps the target pixels in memory. The fit itself is unchanged

predefined_depth_path default None -> '' so that --predefined_depth_path parses (with None argparse types it NoneType and rejects every value: 'invalid NoneType value'); '' is falsy, so the reader's own test 'if use_predefined_depth and predefined_depth_path' is unchanged

changes.order_4_2: input reading: prior depth incl. masking of no-hit pixels (order 5.5 2)
changes.what: with --use_predefined_depth the per-view min-max normalisation of the prior depth and of the rendered depth is taken over the loss's own mask (original_depth > 0 = the prior-hit pixels) and is 0 outside it (official: over the whole image, which with a partial prior would put the prior's minimum at 0 and compare two differently normalised depths); the rest of the depth loss is the official line (mean over all pixels, so a no-hit pixel weighs 0); a view-iteration whose hit pixels cannot be normalised (prior or render constant on them) has no depth loss and is counted (jbgs_depth_skipped.jsonl)

jbgs_cameras.json (the training and evaluation views the run uses), jbgs_train_log.jsonl every 100 iterations (loss terms, depth weight, Gaussians, PyTorch memory), jbgs_train_summary.json; a NaN loss raises and stops (order 3.7); any stop writes jbgs_stop.json (iteration, image, Gaussians, PyTorch memory, nvidia-smi, traceback; order 4.10) and re-raises

changes.order_4_2: version pinning in the Docker build
changes.what: the repository's prebuilt binaries are deleted; the image rebuilds the rasterizer and simple-knn for sm_86 from the in-repo sources

not_changed: the alignment (optimize_depth: Adam lr 1.0, decay 0.8 per 100 steps, stop rule, 0.1 % prune, reprojection-error weights)
the loss 0.8 L1 + 0.2 (1 - SSIM) + mean(|gt - render * mask| * confidence) * 0.6 exp(-150 L_align)
densification, optimiser, learning rates, iterations, test and save iterations
the renderer and its depth out_depth = D / A
split_index.json and the scene files are inputs (cdgs_scenes.py), not code

deviations.data_device: cuda (default): --data_device cpu raises at official train.py line 133 (depth * depth_mask: the CUDA render times the mask on the data device), prep/cdgs/envcheck.json; order 5.2 3 keeps the default then
deviations.seed: the official train.py does not fix a seed (safe_state(args.quiet) is commented out); only np.random.seed(42) in the split reader. Runs are not bit-reproducible; no seed is added (order 4.2)
deviations.pipeline_debug: PipelineParams.debug defaults to True in CDGS (copies every rasterizer input to the CPU before each call for its error dump); kept in training; the post-processing renders with debug False (same values)
deviations.test_renders: training_report writes the test renders to a path built from model_path.split('/') that drops the leading '/', so they land under <working dir>/ph/... (official behaviour, kept)
deviations.debug_dir: debug/ (relative) in the working directory = the run folder; aligned depths and PNGs per training view (official default debug_output True)
deviations.allocator: no PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF for CDGS: torch 2.0.1 rejects expandable_segments ('Unrecognized CachingAllocator option', runner test 10-15); the fork-image steps (run_gpu_bl.sh) keep it

changes.what: alignment targets: a training view uses only the SfM points it observed (its 2-D observations in the scene's images.bin; tracks restricted to the training views as before) instead of every point projected into every view; the reprojection-error weights, the per-view max-normalisation, the 0.1 % prune, Adam (lr 1.0, x0.8 per 100 steps) and the stopping rule are unchanged
changes.why: the official target map has no visibility test: at scale 1 / shift 0, 55-80 % of the v1 targets lay > 1 m behind the prior surface and carried 93-99.9 % of the weighted alignment loss (prep/cdgs/v1_official_alignment)

changes.what: units: the alignment runs on the prior (source) and SfM (target) depths divided by s = the site's median own-observation target depth / TT, so L_align and the weight 0.6 exp(-150 L_align) are in the authors' data scale; the aligned depth is multiplied back by s, so the confidence map and the per-view min-max normalised depth loss are computed on metres exactly as in v1
